issue: #628 — the descriptor repoint's carried sign-off item: 'the deposit arm's ExUnits are not unconditional (l2_datum is unbounded); both arms' frontiers get measured and recorded post-regeneration'. Carried to the #617 sign-off checklist.
spec: GOAL_SPEC §5.3 and §5.5.3: the LedgerOutputCommitmentV1 descriptor is the sole utxos_root trie value, so validate_valid_deposit_transition and apply_l2_outputs both pay for descriptor derivation, and §3.3 fixes the execution basis they are judged at.
purpose: Post-regeneration ExUnits frontier for the two arms #628 repointed onto LedgerOutputCommitmentV1 plus the isolated §5.3 descriptor derivation they both pay for. Unlike version 1 of this artifact this is a GATE: every row is re-measured by scripts/verify-transition-trace-descriptor-exec-ledger-v1.mjs, every crossing is a bracket between adjacent MEASURED rows rather than an interpolation, and every arm-cost claim is a difference against a fixture-only baseline that the verifier recomputes.
note:
2026-09-29 remeasurement with pinned v1.1.23+5adf783 under testnet. Raw Aiken test readings include fixture construction; arm cost claims use only the recomputed differences against matching fixture-only rows. No execution basis was changed. The measured whole-test descriptor crossing is now bracketed by 2,819 and 3,083 output CBOR bytes; the deposit crossing is between 66 and 134 serialised datum bytes. The original presence-only deposit crossing and the earlier descriptor brackets are retired. These are measured adjacent rungs, not interpolated limits or complete transaction-fit claims. The marginal descriptor row at 3,083 bytes still exceeds the basis, and the output-width policy question remains open.

Source changes since the original recording include canonical empty-byte datum support (3e3090aa1) and authenticated transition continuations (13ff70d63). The compiler change from 2a78108 to 5adf783 moves none of these rows: at 89663a0db, 5adf783 reproduces the original readings exactly. The drop is 13ff70d63's rewrite of `ledger_output_summaries_v1` in `lib/midgard/script-context-v1.ak`, which summarises an output's value, datum and reference script once and reuses them for both encodings, instead of re-summarising the whole TxOut twice. That saves about 720K mem per descriptor derivation and about 1.0M per deposit-arm derivation. It removes no check: decoding, the materialisability check and `descriptor_is_well_formed` run unchanged, and `consolidated_ledger_output_summaries_match_the_separate_entry_points` and the golden descriptor vectors pin the same summaries. The deposit rows fall by less than that, because 89427ff46 later authenticates deposits from event-history evidence (+605K mem on `deposit_arm_datum_absent`). `historicalMeasurement` keeps the original figures. The empty-inline-datum control now asserts successful derivation. The proof.test no-op fixture additionally shares an identical output descriptor and independently builds its expected root in this remeasurement; its reduced whole-test cost is fixture work and is not a validator speedup. The separate frontier arm/baseline pair still measures validator marginal cost.

Re-taken the same day at 9993b316e, after `script_value_data` began re-sorting each policy's asset names by their bytes, the order the script context uses. The sort is paid wherever a descriptor is derived through the one-shot path, and its cost grows with the number of asset names: deriving the descriptor of an output with no native assets costs 666 mem more, the three-asset `builds_rich_multi_chunk_output_exactly` vector 27,850 mem more, each deposit-arm derivation 9,546 mem more, and the L2 no-op arm's marginal cost falls by 134 mem. No fit judgement and no crossing bracket moves.

Each module is measured in its own focused invocation, with nonzero selected test counts and all listed neutralisation controls required to pass.
readingKind: Whole-test upper bounds. See `note`, paragraph one: no raw row on this lane is a validator cost, and the `marginal` block is the only place an arm cost is stated.

compiler.why: The patched fork, not stock v1.1.22: the stock compiler that ships the blueprint has a live unsound codegen bug, so a reading taken with it would not be a reading of the code this tree ships.

measurement.workingTreeChanges: The asset-name sort that `script_value_data` in `lib/midgard/script-context-v1.ak` now applies to the one-shot output Value, with the test changes committed alongside it. See `note`, paragraph three.
measurement.harness: Every reading is taken through onchain/aiken/scripts/run-focused-check.mjs via exec-ledger-measure-v1.mjs, the repo's mandated reading path: it asserts the collected module is the one asked for and that every selected test passed, so a row for a test that did not run — or one that did not pass — cannot appear here. No reading was taken by spawning Aiken directly.

basis.source: GOAL_SPEC §3.3, as exported by GOAL_SPEC_EXECUTION_BASIS_V1 in onchain/aiken/scripts/exec-ledger-within-basis-v1.mjs — 20% margin off the supported L1 floor MIDGARD_CONSENSUS_LIMITS_V1.minSupportedL1MaxTxMemoryUnits of 16,500,000 mem. The verifier reads the basis from that module and never from this file.

modules.sweep: descriptor_output_cbor_bytes — a canonical output whose only varying part is an inline datum, so the axis is output size at fixed shape. `sizeBytes` is the output's exact CBOR length and each row asserts it on chain rather than being labelled here.
modules.neutralisationNote: Controls pin exact fixture widths, truncated-output refusal, output-index binding and successful canonical empty-inline-datum derivation.

descriptor_3083_bytes_derives.infeasibility: The widest rung measured, 3,083 CBOR bytes, reads 13,492,204 mem whole-test and 13,363,357 net of its fixture-only twin: 102.2% and 101.2% of the basis. It is the first measured rung over the basis on both readings; 2,819 bytes fits on both. The ladder stops here because the curve is linear at about 2,965 mem per output byte and a wider rung adds evidence but no new fact.
descriptor_3083_bytes_derives.ruling: #628 sign-off item, #617 wave. Whether §5.3 owes a maximum serviceable output width is the open question this rung informs; see `openQuestions` (`maximum-serviceable-output-width`).

modules.sweep: deposit_arm_l2_datum_bytes — the serialised width of the deposit's `l2_datum`, which is the one field of a deposit a user controls and the field #628 flagged as unbounded. `sizeBytes` 0 means the field is ABSENT; 2 is a present one-byte blob. The mapping from rung to serialised width is pinned on chain by `deposit_datum_cbor_lengths_are_exact` rather than asserted here. The two `l2_no_op_arm` rows are not part of that sweep and carry `sizeBytes` 0 for that reason.
modules.neutralisationNote: A cost row over an arm that accepts everything measures nothing. `deposit_arm_rejects_arbitrary_projected_value` shows the deposit arm still returns False when the projected value is not the descriptor it must be; `l2_arm_refuses_full_output_replay` shows the L2 arm still aborts rather than replaying full output bytes into utxos_root, which is the #628 hole itself. `deposit_datum_cbor_lengths_are_exact` pins the axis every crossing below is expressed on.

deposit_arm_datum_128_bytes.infeasibility: Whole-test 13,477,442 mem against a 13,200,000 basis, 102.1%; marginal 7,069,083, 53.6%, within. The first chunked rung: two 64-byte chunks inside an indefinite byte string. The whole-test crossing sits between this rung and the 66-byte one, and it is fixture cost, because the fixture serialises the datum three times: into the deposit info under the deposits root, into the reference input's inline datum and into the projected output the descriptor is derived from.
deposit_arm_datum_128_bytes.ruling: #628 sign-off item, #617 wave; see the `marginal` block.

deposit_arm_datum_256_bytes.infeasibility: The widest rung measured: whole-test 14,290,622 mem against a 13,200,000 basis, 108.3%. Marginal 7,467,181, 56.6% of the basis and within. Across the one-byte to 266-byte rungs the marginal cost rises by 714,836 mem and the whole-test reading by 1,528,150, because fixture growth is charged to the row as well. The ledger does not extrapolate past this rung.
deposit_arm_datum_256_bytes.ruling: #628 sign-off item, #617 wave. Whether §5.3 owes an explicit `l2_datum` width bound is the open question this ladder informs; see `openQuestions`.

l2_no_op_arm.infeasibility: The L2 no-op transition arm — one spent and one produced Ada-only output, two descriptor derivations — reads 13,536,775 mem whole-test against a 13,200,000 basis, 102.6%. It is an upper bound on a test, not on `apply_l2_outputs`: the fixture-only twin reads 8,336,229, so the arm's marginal cost is 5,200,546 mem, 39.4% of the basis. #628 carried the original reading, 15,289,803, to the sign-off; see `historicalMeasurement`.
l2_no_op_arm.ruling: #628 sign-off item, #617 wave. The marginal figure is within basis, so this row records a harness cost and not an infeasibility of the validator.

adjacentMinorsVerifiedAtHead.statusAtHead: Historical observation at bdcb7d16; not reverified by the 2026-09-29 execution remeasurement.
adjacentMinorsVerifiedAtHead.detail: bdcb7d16 rewrote the it.each block formerly titled 'preserves the Aiken tag-4 output encoding for $label' into 'refuses to replay $label, which has no canonical ledger value'. The old body asserted that detectTransitionTraceFaults produced no l2_transaction_transition_matches_authenticated_replay detection for those shapes — i.e. that the tag-4 encoder round-tripped them byte for byte. The new body asserts a missingWitnessData rejection instead. The round-trip property is now only stated in the block's comment ('the Aiken tag-4 encoder neither reorders nor re-canonicalises them'); no assertion in the suite still pins it, and the case that lost the most coverage (opaque native-script bytes) was additionally split out into its own refusal test at :1233 documenting the parse_script_ref divergence, which is wave item 9 / #633.
adjacentMinorsVerifiedAtHead.measurementAdjacency: It removes the only executable check that the tag-4 encoding is stable across the encoder, which is the input every descriptor reading in this artifact is derived from.

adjacentMinorsVerifiedAtHead.statusAtHead: Historical observation at bdcb7d16; not reverified by the 2026-09-29 execution remeasurement.
adjacentMinorsVerifiedAtHead.detail: ledgerTrieValue wraps buildCanonicalMidgardLedgerEntryOutputMaterialV1 in a bare try/catch that returns the raw output bytes on any throw. Its comment justifies this for fixtures that deliberately feed non-canonical outputs, which have no descriptor. The catch is untyped and unconditional, so a genuine regression in the descriptor encoder — for any fixture, not just the deliberately-malformed ones — silently rebuilds the fixture's utxos_root from full output bytes, which is exactly the pre-#628 shape the repoint removed, and the suite can still go green over it.
adjacentMinorsVerifiedAtHead.measurementAdjacency: The same encoder is the off-chain twin of the on-chain builder every row in this artifact measures; a silent fallback means a cross-language divergence in it would not surface here. The formerly unsupported empty inline datum illustrates the class of behavior that a fallback could hide; that descriptor case is now supported.

resolvedQuestions.resolution: Resolved by 3e3090aa1: canonical empty byte strings now materialize and derive a ledger descriptor. The derivation_accepts_an_empty_inline_datum control pins this behavior.

blueprint.note: The blueprint is not an input to an `aiken check` reading; it is recorded so the reading is bound to the same regenerated source tree the #617 wave signs off. The two measurement modules this lane adds are test modules and move it by zero bytes.

historicalMeasurement.harness: Every reading is taken through onchain/aiken/scripts/run-focused-check.mjs via exec-ledger-measure-v1.mjs, the repo's mandated reading path: it asserts the collected module is the one asked for and that every selected test passed, so a row for a test that did not run — or one that did not pass — cannot appear here. No reading was taken by spawning Aiken directly.
historicalMeasurement.environment: MIDGARD_AIKEN_ENV=testnet. `env/default.ak` and `env/testnet.ak` differ only in `shift_duration` (30 against 3,600,000), which at least one pinned row here — `accepts_out_of_window_deposit_fault` — is sensitive to, so the verifier must be run with the same environment or its readings are readings of a different program. Every command below carries it.
historicalMeasurement.memoryCap: Every measurement run was taken under `ulimit -v 16777216`. No run approached it: the widest peaked at 740,100 KB resident.
historicalMeasurement.slotDiscipline: One `aiken` process machine-wide; every run in this lane waited on `pgrep -c -x aiken` reaching 0 before starting.
historicalMeasurement.determinism: The descriptor rows were taken twice in two separate invocations and reproduced to the unit.
historicalMeasurement.reproductionFidelity: The two sweep modules rebuild the fixtures of `accepts_valid_deposit_transition_fault` and `accepts_valid_l2_transaction_no_op_transition_fault` rather than importing them (a private `fn` in a `.test` module is not importable). The reproduction is faithful to within the record wrapper the sweep adds: `deposit_arm_datum_absent` reads 12,791,247 against the original's 12,776,094 (+15,153 mem, 0.12%) and `l2_no_op_arm` reads 15,289,803 against 15,279,779 (+10,024, 0.07%). Both originals are pinned as rows here, so the two can never drift apart unnoticed.
